A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diffusion is a key factor in determining the dynamics of membrane domains.
the diffusion constant of the smallest domains is the limiting factor for the rate of domain growth and dissolution.
the diffusion constant is not the only factor that influences dissolution/growth, but it is a significant one, especially in highly confined geometries.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the diffusion of clusters and small domains of lipid molecules can play a role in the dynamics of domain dissolution/growth, and that the diffusion of such small domains is affected by the geometry of the environment.
the diffusion of small domains is a significant factor in the dynamics of dissolution and growth of membrane domains.

diffusion constants are not always the best measure of domain dynamics and that the geometry of the domain environment can influence the diffusion of membrane components and thus the dynamics of membrane domains.
